title: Incremental runway + sprint gating for Quarterly hosted API & model catalog
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Objective: Define and operationalize a lightweight, incremental quarterly runway that ties OKRs to concrete sprint-level gates for Hosted API endpoints and the model catalog. This ticket scopes the gating rules, signal thresholds, rollout windows, and cross-team handoffs needed for safe incremental rollouts of model variants and hosted endpoint changes. Motivation: teams need a repeatable way to move from discovery -> canary -> staged rollout -> full commit while preserving latency and cost SLOs and preventing model-quality regressions. Deliverables: (1) gate matrix doc with signals and thresholds, (2) sprint checklist templates for PM/Eng/Design, (3) dashboard widgets and alerts for canary health, (4) playbook snippets for rollback and capacity-hedge triggers. Constraints: must be implementable with existing Console dashboards and Runtime observability hooks in the next quarter; minimize new infra work. Success: teams can ship model swaps and endpoint changes with predictable windows and measurable guardrails that surface regressions before customer impact.
acceptance_criteria: Gate matrix published that maps OKR signoffs to technical signals (latency p95, error rate, token cost delta, eval-quality regression) and explicit threshold values
Sprint gating checklist created and templatized for PM/Eng/Design with ownership, required artifacts and rollback plan
Console dashboard recipe (list of metrics + alert thresholds) documented and validated with Observability team
At least one internal pilot rollout executed using the gating playbook: results captured and retrospective completed
Dependencies identified and owners assigned for any infra gaps; rollout path has mitigation steps if infra changes exceed scope
Post-release runbook and ticket template for incident/quality regressions added to repo and referenced from the gate matrix
notes: Design input: require a simple visual state machine in Console to represent gate status (Draft -> Canary -> Staged -> Committed -> Rollback)
We should reuse existing canary windows (2h, 24h, 72h) but allow product teams to opt into longer windows for high-risk models
Suggest a small set of default thresholds for model quality regressions derived from historical eval deltas; PMs can tune per endpoint
Consider a 'capacity hedge' flag that reserves burst capacity on Dedicated pools during staged rollouts to avoid throttling surprises
